text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States, Japanese embassy and European Union condemn police brutality directed against opposition leaders.
- The government blames opposition leaders over recent incidents where police used excessive force against them.
- Thirty-nine opposition parliamentarians reject President Daniel arap Moi's directive to resettle 700 families who were victims of clashes in the Rift Valley.
- Armed thugs break into the home of opposition Democratic Party of Kenya Chairman Mwai Kibaki.
- Nairobi City Council may hike water charges by 40 percent to raise cash to pay off a foreign firm contracted to build one of the dams that will supply the city with water.
- The Electoral Commission says voter registration will be delayed because of a lack of computer facilities.
- A woman suspected of being the mastermind behind a drug syndicate in Nairobi is arrested.
- Business tycoon Kamlesh Pattni returns from a three-day trip to Europe.
- The Registrar of Societies reinstates Chibule wa Tsuma as the chairman of the opposition Kenya National Congress party. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
